children: Jayatri Nag Kolkata: Calling CJP leaders and members 'cockroaches' and comparing them with 'coronavirus', West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday said there was a need to weed out the influence of 'Dimagi Naxals' and 'tukde tukde' gang on the minds of students.

Adhikari vowed to ignite patriotism and nationalistic feelings among students through debates and cultural activities. The chief minister was speaking to mediapersons in Purba Medinipur's Ramnagar where he had gone to meet family members of those who died in the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal stampede on October 17. "To make students patriotic, every year, debate, quiz competitions, impromptu speeches should be started in schools.

Then only the bed bugs, cockroaches, Dimagi naxals, tuke tukde gang and the Azadi-in-Kashmir gang-all these elements can be defeated," Adhikari said. The state government is also looking at reintroducing the 'pass-fail' system in schools, he said.

It was stopped by the earlier Left and TMC governments and students were promoted even if they failed. This largely impacted the education system and learning of students, experts believe. Adhikari also said using mobile phones in school would be barred. "I am against mobile phone usage in schools. I have already told the education ministers," the CM said.

He said the state government is eyeing introduction of tablets for educational purposes, bringing major syllabus change and implementing NEP and introducing NCC in the coming days. The scheme for buying mobile phones for students was introduced by the previous Trinamool government during Covid. He also indicated an entire change in syllabus and emphasis laid on the history of Bengal and India. Adhikari also claimed that chapters about "those who drove out Tata Motors from Singur in school history books during the Trinamool regime, referring to former CM Mamata Banerjee and the anti-land acquisition agitations" will not be taught. Bratachari, a socio-cultural and spiritual movement founded in 1932 in undivided Bengal, would also be brought back, he said.

title: CM Adhikari Vows to Ignite Patriotism and Nationalistic Feelings among Students
